chapter: Clarence Williams's 1936 article and the dispute
title: Article continued: early recording bands and imitators of the ODJB
summary: The reading lists early recording bands and Clarence Williams's Blue Five; La Rocca says Fletcher Henderson copied the Dixieland Jazz Band records.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Go ahead. The man who took it from King Oliver and added the plunger was Johnny Dunn, who was with Mamie Smith's Jazz Hounds and Lou Leslie's Plantation Review. It's a continuation all of the same quote. The first recording bands were the Dixieland Jazz Band. Go ahead. W.C. Smith... He played no jazz. I wonder who W.C. Smith is. Could that be Joseph Smith?

Well, Paul Whiteman, Kid Tua Jazz. Mamie Smith and her jazz hands. I have them records of all of them. Clarence Williams' Blue Five and the Clarence Williams' Blue Rhythm Band, which was featuring Louis Armstrong, Donald Redmond, that's spelled R-E-D-M-O-N-D, Busta Bailey, Coleman Hawkins, etc. Louis Armstrong's first record that brought him recognition was Everybody Loves My Baby, which he recorded with the Clarence Williams' Blue Five. Fletcher Henderson and Benny Morton of Kansas City were also...
They were imitators of the Dixieland Jazz Band. Fletcher Henderson was one of the first colored men to copy from the records of the Dixieland Jazz Band.
Fletcher Henderson and Benny Morton of Kansas City were also among the first swing artists. Benny Morton's name is spelled M-O-R-T-O-N. Do you want me to read the letter to the editor? Just a moment.
